raw_text: Hi — I'm the independent reviewer (member_002). Please publish your exact final fixed candidate with fix_patch and send me a handoff_patch when ready; I'll adopt it, run same-version public tests, and accept or request changes. Meanwhile I'm reading the relevant code so my review is grounded.

Final fixed candidate is published as patch-1 (source version v5, files_sha256 7042c5b0...). Please integrate_patch, run public tests on that exact content, then org_review_patch accept or request_changes.

What changed:
- seaborn/_core/scales.py, Continuous._setup: legend labels are built with `formatter.format_ticks(locs)`, which drops the shared offset that ScalarFormatter (e.g. `$\times\mathdefault{10^{6}}\mathdefault{}$`) normally shows beside the axis. Legends have no axis, so the multiplicative offset was lost and a pointsize/color variable around 1e6 was described with plain "2.0"-style labels. The fix queries `getattr(formatter, "get_offset", lambda: "")()` and appends the offset to every label when non-empty; labels are unchanged when the formatter reports no offset. It also drops NaN tick locations and casts locs to float, because an Int64 dtype breaks get_offset/format_ticks.
- tests/_core/test_scales.py: added `PointSize` import; new `TestContinuous::test_legend_labels_include_offset` (float values ~1e6 with PointSize -> labels keep the 1e6 offset) and `TestContinuous::test_legend_labels_without_offset` (small-range data -> no offset appended).

My same-version public evidence: tests/_core/test_scales.py + tests/_core/test_plot.py -> 258 passed, 6 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 errors (report test-report-9107e270abb910bf46d32dec, source v5). Note the two new test names contain "legend", so a `-k legend` filter also covers them. Independent verification is yours; I will run the final integration tests again on my own tree after your review.

ACCEPT recorded for patch-1 (review-1, event sequence 57). No changes requested.

Evidence: I independently integrated patch-1 (zero conflicts, my workspace v2, files_sha256 7042c5b041e5cd8773033c8386b0d70eb61922cf70f35a7ea375356d2ee75747) and ran public tests on that exact content: tests/_core/test_scales.py + tests/_core/test_plot.py => 264 collected, 258 passed, 6 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 errors, exitstatus 0, validation_status=verified (my report test-report-9e8f2d0f14e08e6924221ea4). Both new tests passed, including test_legend_labels_include_offset and the negative control test_legend_labels_without_offset; existing label/unit/base/like, log and symlog tick tests still pass.

Code assessment: appending formatter.get_offset() to each legend label after format_ticks(locs) correctly restores $\times\mathdefault{10^{6}}\mathdefault{}$ that legends silently dropped; getattr guard keeps LogFormatterSciNotation / EngFormatter / label= callables safe, and the empty-offset check leaves labels unchanged when no multiplier applies. The ~np.isnan + astype(float) on locs is a reasonable robustness addition.

One residual note (not blocking): because the fix delegates entirely to matplotlib's get_offset(), the rcParams the issue mentions (axes.formatter.useoffset, axes.formatter.offset_threshold) are inherited rather than explicitly handled — worth a sentence in the PR/commit description, but not a code problem.

Next step is yours: your final working tree is the code endpoint, so integrate patch-1 into your own tree if not already there, then run_tests, fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Ping me only if you publish a different candidate, since any new version needs a fresh review.
